title: Prod rollout phase 1 (us-east): enable perf-canary on initial model set + monitoring + sign-off
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- First production region rollout for perf-canary (always-on synthetic workload) to detect per-model p95 latency regressions and tokens/sec drops with low noise.
- Phase 1 scope: us-east only, small model set (2–3), warning alerts only initially, then enable paging after threshold tuning + SRE sign-off.

Rollout scope (phase 1)
- Region: us-east
- Tier: Hosted (shared) + Dedicated pool signal coverage only if it does not increase cardinality (see label set)
- Hardware SKU: H100-80GB (primary). A100 coverage deferred to phase 2 unless we see high variance.
- Canary models (initial)
  1) llama-3.1-8b-instruct (top model, high traffic)
  2) qwen2.5-7b-instruct (top model, recent scheduler changes)
  3) mistral-small-24b-instruct (high-risk: new kernel selection path)
- Workload profile: synthetic prompt distribution v0 (length buckets + prefill/decode mix), seedable for reproducibility; no customer prompts.

Success criteria / exit criteria
- Canary overhead stays within budget: <0.5% GPU capacity in us-east for covered models (validate via QPS cap + observed GPU utilization deltas).
- Metrics emitted and queryable with stable label set (no cardinality blowups): model, model_version, runtime_build_id, kernel_id, region, sku, tier (tier optional; only if it does not explode label space).
- Baselines fetched correctly for (model + model_version + runtime_build_id + sku + region), with clear fallback behavior (no baseline => no paging, only "baseline_missing" warn).
- Warning alerts fire only on real regressions (target: <1 false positive/day/model after first week of tuning).
- On-call runbook works end-to-end: alerts include dashboard links + baseline comparison + likely attribution hints (queueing vs execution, kernel tag changes).
- SRE sign-off to enable paging after a minimum 7-day bake with warning-only alerts.

Implementation/operational checklist (phase 1)
1) Deployment
- [x] Deploy perf-canary to us-east via Helm + Terraform (service account + secrets).
- [x] Ensure canary uses restricted auth scope (internal inference read only; no write paths).
- [x] Set QPS caps + concurrency limit to enforce overhead budget.
- [x] Confirm safe-disable switch (feature flag / config) works and does not impact inference endpoints.

2) Configuration
- [x] Control-plane config updated with canary model allowlist for us-east.
- [x] Threshold config loaded for initial models (start conservative; warn-only).
- [x] Minimum sample size + evaluation window configured (avoid flapping on low traffic).

3) Observability
- [x] Dashboards: per-model p50/p95/p99 e2e latency, runtime-only latency, prefill/decode split, queueing time, tokens/sec, batch size distribution; baseline overlay.
- [x] Alert payload includes: model, model_version, runtime_build_id, sku, observed vs baseline, percent delta, confidence/min-sample status, and links.
- [x] Incident-bot formatting verified (dedupe key includes model+region+sku+metric; no spam).

4) Validation
- [x] Validate instrumentation correctness: queueing-time and batch-size distribution look sane under load.
- [x] Validate kernel/runtime tags are present and stable across deploys.
- [x] Verify telemetry pipeline latency (alerts should arrive within the expected window; flag if ingestion delays >10m).

5) Rollout plan
- Day 0–2: Deploy + metrics only (no alerts) to confirm stability.
- Day 3–7: Enable warning alerts; tune thresholds/dampening.
- Day 8+: Enable paging for top model(s) only after SRE + runtime sign-off.

- Baseline/threshold ADR (Confluence): /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-perf-canary-baseline-and-thresholds
- Dashboards spec (Confluence): /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/perf-canary-dashboards-spec
- Alerting policy (Confluence): /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/per-model-latency-slos-and-alerting-policy

Owners / sign-off
- Runtime TL: Noah Patel
- Scheduling: Sofia Ivanova
- Kernels: Hiro Tanaka
- Telemetry: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
- SRE sign-off: Sean Gallagher (primary), Rafael Mendes (routing)

Notes
- Phase 1 intentionally avoids broad region fanout and avoids adding high-cardinality labels (e.g., customer_id, route_id). If we need Dedicated pool visibility, do it via separate dashboards/queries keyed by pool_id with tight allowlist.
- Any sustained regression caught by canary during this phase should auto-trigger a rollout pause request to #eng-releases (manual until PM-642 gating work lands).
comments: 2026-01-20 (Talia Benson): Created phase-1 rollout ticket for us-east. Requesting owners to confirm initial model list + hardware SKU and agree on warning-only period before paging.

2026-01-22 (Noah Patel): Proposed initial models: llama-3.1-8b-instruct, qwen2.5-7b-instruct, mistral-small-24b-instruct. Rationale: (1) top traffic, (2) scheduler changes last week, (3) recent kernel selection updates. Confirmed canary prompts are synthetic shapes only; no customer data.

2026-01-23 (Logan Wright): Telemetry pipeline ready. Reminder: keep labels limited to model/model_version/runtime_build_id/kernel_id/region/sku. Avoid tier unless we can guarantee bounded values. Will monitor ingestion delay; if >10m we should suppress alerting to avoid late pages.

2026-01-24 (Allison Grant): Please ensure alert payload includes direct Grafana links and runbook link, and the dedupe key is stable. If alerts are too chatty, we’ll adjust dampening/min-samples before enabling paging.

2026-01-27 (Nadia Rahman): Baseline artifacts for us-east H100 generated from controlled load. Noted higher variance on mistral-small prefill latency; recommend higher min-sample and wider thresholds initially.

2026-01-29 (Sean Gallagher): SRE ask: run a safe-disable drill in us-east before turning on any paging. Also confirm canary overhead via GPU utilization panel; we need confidence it stays <0.5% even during peak.

2026-02-01 (Noah Patel): Deployed perf-canary to us-east (metrics only). Verified runtime_build_id + kernel_id tags present. Queueing-time metric shows expected behavior under burst (peaks during autoscaler lag).
2026-02-03 (Rafael Mendes): Incident-bot handler is deduping correctly in #incidents for synthetic test alerts. Routing for warning alerts goes to #eng-runtime; paging stays disabled for now.
2026-02-05 (Noah Patel): Enabled warning alerts for llama-3.1-8b and qwen2.5-7b. Left mistral-small in metrics-only due to baseline variance; will add after 48h of stability.

2026-02-07 (Sofia Ivanova): Review: queueing vs execution breakdown looks actionable. One transient warning correlated with batch-size distribution shift; no customer impact. Suggest increasing min-samples for tokens/sec signal to avoid noise at low QPS.

2026-02-09 (Hiro Tanaka): Kernel tag attribution works. Verified alerts include kernel_id delta when selection changes. Requested follow-up: add explicit "kernel_change_detected" annotation in payload (not blocking phase-1).

2026-02-10 (Noah Patel): Safe-disable drill completed (feature flag). Canary stopped sending traffic; no inference endpoint impact. Overhead estimate in us-east: ~0.28% GPU capacity for the two enabled models at current caps.

2026-02-12 (Sean Gallagher): SRE sign-off to enable paging for llama-3.1-8b only, after 7-day warning bake. Condition: keep dampening window and min-samples as currently configured; revisit after first page.

2026-02-14 (Noah Patel): Enabled paging for llama-3.1-8b in us-east (Sev2 for sustained p95 + tokens/sec regression beyond threshold). Phase-1 rollout complete. Next: expand model coverage (ENG-4881) and incorporate learnings into noise-reduction backlog (ENG-4882).
